subject: [Review] Burst pool fleet topology + networking constraints (need routing/control-plane sign-off)
related_links: Confluence: Burst pool provisioning and topology
ADR-0142: Burst admission control and cooldowns
body:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nina Petrova <nina.petrova@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Keiko Yamamoto <keiko.yamamoto@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 12, 2025 at 9:14 AM
Subject: [Review] Burst pool fleet topology + networking constraints (need routing/control-plane sign-off)

Hi all — sharing the current proposal for how we provision and isolate Dedicated “burst pools” per region/GPU type.

Attachments:
- burst-pools-topology-v3.pdf
- burst_topology_v3.png
- burst-egress-acl-matrix-v1.xlsx

TL;DR / what I need from you:
1) Routing sign-off (Mina): can you confirm the data plane can consume the capacity/eligibility signals with this topology, and that fallback semantics (baseline → burst → deny/fallback) don’t require cross-cluster hops we can’t support?
2) Control-plane sign-off (Ethan/Jordan): confirm policy evaluation + config distribution model works with separate burst pool “fleet IDs” and doesn’t assume same-cluster scheduling.
3) Fleet sign-off (Vanessa): confirm this doesn’t collide with baseline Dedicated guarantees and keeps hosted commitments isolated.

Proposed topology (v3):
- Each region has:
  - Dedicated baseline pools (tenant-reserved) — unchanged
  - Burst shared pools (region + GPU type) — NEW, shared across eligible Dedicated tenants
- Burst pools are provisioned as separate node pools with:
  - Distinct pool labels: pool_type=burst, burst_pool_id=<region>:<gpu>
  - Separate autoscaling guardrails (cooldowns, circuit breakers handled in control plane / routing gates)
  - Explicit exclusion from reservation allocation / baseline schedulers

Networking / isolation constraints (non-negotiables from infra + security):
- No direct east/west network path from burst pools into baseline tenant subnets.
  - Burst serving nodes only reach:
    - Redwood control plane endpoints (policy + config)
    - Model artifact store
    - Telemetry sinks
- Request payloads in burst pools are treated the same as hosted fleet (no additional data exposure), but must still respect:
  - Region residency constraints (no cross-region bursting)
  - Tenant isolation at request layer (authn/z + per-tenant headers/claims)
- We do NOT support “spillover” from burst pool back to baseline cluster mid-request (no cross-cluster failover once admitted). Routing must decide prior to admission.

Open question I want to settle this week:
- Do we place burst pools in the same k8s cluster as hosted, or separate clusters per region?
  - v3 assumes separate cluster per region for burst pools (reduces blast radius, cleaner ACLs), but still shares some core infra (artifact cache, telemetry).
  - If routing requires co-location with hosted for service discovery reasons, we need to document exactly what’s needed.

Target: I’m trying to lock topology by Tue 6/17 so ENG-4825 can proceed without churn.

Thanks,
Irene

—
Irene Choi
Cluster Architecture
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Nina Petrova <nina.petrova@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Keiko Yamamoto <keiko.yamamoto@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 12, 2025 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: [Review] Burst pool fleet topology + networking constraints (need routing/control-plane sign-off)

This generally matches what we want.

Fleet notes:
- Strong +1 on separate node pools + explicit labels. We should also add an admission-time sanity check that a “baseline reservation” never binds to pool_type=burst (belt + suspenders).
- Separate clusters for burst is fine for us operationally, BUT we’ll need to be explicit about who owns cluster lifecycle/oncall. If it’s “burst = hosted-like,” then hosted oncall needs visibility, otherwise Dedicated oncall will get paged for a hosted-ish issue.
- In us-west-2 we can stand up A100 + H100 burst pools; in eu-central-1 likely H100 only in the first cut (supply).

One request: can you add to the doc a single section called “What hosted is protected from” and list the hard boundaries (quota, network, routing gates). It will come up in approval.

-Vanessa


-----

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Nina Petrova <nina.petrova@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Keiko Yamamoto <keiko.yamamoto@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 12, 2025 at 11:27 AM
Subject: Re: [Review] Burst pool fleet topology + networking constraints (need routing/control-plane sign-off)

Thanks — this is close to what routing assumed in the ENG-4824 design.

Routing constraints / requirements:
- We need burst pool discovery to look like a separate “fleet” with its own endpoints and health. We should NOT rely on cross-cluster service discovery to find burst backends.
- Decision point must be prior to request admission. Agree: no mid-flight spillover.
- We can support “baseline → burst → (same-region) fallback model variant” as long as:
  1) policy engine returns deterministic deny reason codes (for logs + customer error semantics)
  2) we have a per-region saturation signal for burst pools (so we can stop attempting burst when it’s clearly full)

On the question of same cluster vs separate cluster:
- Separate clusters are fine. We just need a stable way to publish endpoints + capacity signal into routing.
- If separate clusters, please ensure the endpoint publication mechanism is the same as we use for hosted (or explicitly documented as “burst fleet discovery v1”), otherwise we’ll accumulate one-offs.

Action item for you (if you’re updating the doc): add a quick note on how routing learns:
- burst_fleet_id → list of routable endpoints
- burst_fleet_id → capacity/saturation

Sign-off from routing contingent on that section being explicit.

-Mina


-----

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Nina Petrova <nina.petrova@redwoodinference.com>, Keiko Yamamoto <keiko.yamamoto@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 12, 2025 at 1:06 PM
Subject: Re: [Review] Burst pool fleet topology + networking constraints (need routing/control-plane sign-off)

Control plane perspective:

- Separate fleet IDs is the right abstraction. We already treat “hosted” vs “dedicated” as distinct fleet providers; burst can be another provider with eligibility rules.
- Config distribution: ok as long as fleet_id is included in the policy input (tenant_id, region, model_id, fleet_id). That’s aligned with the draft schema.
- One caveat: we need to ensure policy evaluation doesn’t rely on live cluster calls. It must be cached + deterministic (ADR-0142). So if you’re expecting the policy service to query burst cluster capacity directly, that won’t work.

Proposed interface (from our side):
- Fleet publishes capacity/saturation to a centralized signal store (same one routing uses).
- Policy service uses:
  - tenant config limits
  - allowlist of burst_pool_ids per tenant/region
  - saturation gates (from signal store; cached with TTL)

If the networking constraints require special egress, please confirm whether the policy service endpoint is reachable from burst clusters in private regions without opening new inbound.

We can sign off assuming:
- burst clusters can reach policy + config endpoints
- capacity/saturation is out-of-band (fleet telemetry), not synchronous

-Ethan

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Nina Petrova <nina.petrova@redwoodinference.com>, Keiko Yamamoto <keiko.yamamoto@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 12, 2025 at 1:22 PM
Subject: Re: [Review] Burst pool fleet topology + networking constraints (need routing/control-plane sign-off)

+1 to Ethan.

Two small asks to incorporate:
1) In the ACL matrix, can we explicitly call out that burst pool nodes can’t access Dedicated customer private endpoints (even if in same cloud region)? It’s implied but would be good to say.
2) Add a “failure mode” note:
   - If burst fleet discovery is stale or missing → routing should treat burst as unavailable and stick to baseline/fallback (no retries to burst).

This will help us defend the determinism story when we review with SRE.

-Jordan

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nina Petrova <nina.petrova@redwoodinference.com>, Keiko Yamamoto <keiko.yamamoto@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 13, 2025 at 4:48 PM
Subject: Re: [Review] Burst pool fleet topology + networking constraints (need routing/control-plane sign-off)

Thanks all — incorporated the feedback into v3.1 (same attachments; filenames unchanged in the thread, but content updated).

Updates made:
- Added “Hosted protections / hard boundaries” section (quota + routing gates + network boundaries) per Vanessa.
- Added explicit “Fleet discovery + capacity signal” section per Mina:
  - burst_fleet_id → endpoints (published via existing fleet registry)
  - burst_fleet_id → saturation signals (published via signal store; TTL + caching)
- Clarified that policy does NOT do synchronous cluster calls; uses cached saturation gates per Ethan/ADR-0142.
- Updated ACL matrix wording to explicitly state burst nodes cannot reach Dedicated customer private endpoints (Jordan ask).
- Added failure-mode behavior:
  - stale/missing discovery → treat burst as unavailable; do not attempt

Decision: separate clusters per region for burst pools (not co-located inside hosted clusters). Rationale documented: blast radius + simpler network policy.

Assuming no objections by EOD Mon 6/16, I’ll mark topology as approved and we’ll proceed with ENG-4825 implementation details.

Irene

—
Irene Choi
Cluster Architecture
Redwood Inference
